title: What the Evidence Really Says — Posture, Core Stability, Ergonomics, Stretching and More

hook.en: "Sit up straight or your back will break." "Strengthen your core to fix your pain." "Stretch before every run." Many familiar rules of physiotherapy are weaker than they sound. This lesson does not tear them down for fun: it asks what each claim says, what the research shows, and what you can honestly tell a patient.
hook.ur: "Seedha baithein warna peeth tootegi." "Dard theek karne ke liye core mazboot karein." "Har daur se pehle stretch karein." Physiotherapy ke bohat se jaane pehchane qaide sunne se kamzor hain. Yeh lesson maze ke liye unhein nahi todta: yeh poochhta hai har daawa kya kehta hai, research kya dikhati hai, aur aap mareez ko imaandari se kya bata sakte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll summarise honest evidence on posture and pain, core stability, ergonomics, stretching, foam rolling and "alignment", explain why myths last, and replace a scary or oversimplified message with an accurate, reassuring one.
goal.ur: End tak aap posture aur dard, core stability, ergonomics, stretching, foam rolling aur "alignment" par imaandar saboot ka khulasa karenge, samjhayenge ke afwahein kyun tikti hain, aur daraone ya bohat saade paigham ki jagah durust, tasalli bhara paigham dein ge.

text.en: A myth usually has a **kernel of truth**: slumped posture can feel uncomfortable, and strong muscles help. The problem is **overreach**: turning "can be linked" into "causes damage" and "is common" into "must be fixed". Good evidence-based practice asks three questions of any rule: **Compared with what? How big is the effect? Is it harmful to believe?** Scary beliefs such as "my back is fragile" can themselves keep people in pain.
text.ur: Afwah mein aksar **sachai ka daana** hota hai: jhuki posture takleef deh ho sakti hai, aur mazboot muscles madad karte hain. Masla **hadd se barhna** hai: "juda ho sakta hai" ko "nuqsan karta hai" aur "aam hai" ko "theek karna zaroori hai" bana dena. Achhi evidence-based practice kisi bhi qaide se teen sawal poochhti hai: **Kis ke muqabale mein? Asar kitna bara hai? Kya yeh yaqeen rakhna nuqsan deh hai?** Daraone yaqeen jaise "meri peeth kamzor hai" khud logon ko dard mein rakh sakte hain.

text.en: Think of **old advice from grandparents**: "don't go out with wet hair or you will catch a cold." There is a small truth (feeling cold is unpleasant), but a cold is caused by a virus, not wet hair. Posture advice is often similar: well-meant, partly true and wrongly explained. The kind approach is to keep the care and correct the explanation.
text.ur: **Dada dadi ki purani nasihat** sochein: "geelay baalon ke saath bahar na jao warna sardi lag jayegi." Is mein chhoti si sachai hai (thand lagna takleef deh hai), lekin sardi virus se hoti hai, geelay baalon se nahi. Posture ka mashwara aksar aisa hi hai: neik niyyat, aadhi sach aur ghalat wazahat ke saath. Narmi wala tareeqa care qaim rakhna aur wazahat theek karna hai.

title.en: Common claims and what the evidence supports
title.ur: Aam daawe aur saboot kya himayat karta hai

rows.en: Studies find weak or inconsistent links between slumped sitting or forward head and pain; many pain-free people have "poor" posture
rows.ur: Studies mein jhuki baithak ya aage ke sar aur dard ke beech kamzor ya be-tarteeb talluq milta hai; bohat se be-dard log "kharab" posture rakhte hain

rows.en: "Posture is one of many factors. Change position often, and you do not need to hold yourself rigid."
rows.ur: "Posture bohat se factors mein se ek hai. Position aksar badlein, aur aap ko apne aap ko sakht rakhne ki zaroorat nahi."

rows.en: "Core stability is the key to back pain"
rows.ur: "Core stability peeth dard ki kunji hai"

rows.en: Core exercises help back pain, but about as well as other kinds of exercise; no single type stands out
rows.ur: Core exercises peeth dard mein madad karti hain, lekin doosri qism ki exercise jitni; koi ek qism numaya nahi

rows.en: "Choose exercise you enjoy and will keep doing; core work is a fine option, not the only one."
rows.ur: "Aisi exercise chunein jo aap ko pasand ho aur jari rakh saken; core work achha option hai, wahid nahi."

rows.en: Evidence that chairs and desks alone prevent pain is limited; movement variety and breaks seem to matter
rows.ur: Saboot ke kursi aur desk akele dard rokte hain mehdood hai; harkat ki qismein aur waqfay ahem lagte hain

rows.en: "A comfortable set-up helps, but moving often matters more than the perfect chair."
rows.ur: "Aaramdeh set-up madad karta hai, lekin aksar hilna perfect kursi se zyada ahem hai."

rows.en: "Stretching before exercise prevents injury and soreness"
rows.ur: "Exercise se pehle stretching chot aur dukhan rokti hai"

rows.en: Stretching does not reliably prevent soreness; effects on injury are modest or unclear
rows.ur: Stretching dukhan ko pakke taur par nahi rokti; chot par asar mamooli ya ghair wazeh

rows.en: "Warm up with the activity you will do; stretch if you like it, not because it protects you."
rows.ur: "Jo kaam karne wale hain usi se warm up karein; stretch pasand ho to karein, is liye nahi ke woh bachati hai."

rows.en: Foam rolling may briefly improve flexibility and how sore you feel; effects are small and short and it does not break up tissue
rows.ur: Foam rolling thori der ke liye lachak aur dukhan ke ehsas ko behtar kar sakti hai; asar chhote aur mukhtasar hain aur yeh tissue nahi todti

rows.en: "If it feels good, it is harmless to use, but do not expect to 'fix' tissue."
rows.ur: "Achha lage to istemal karna nuqsan deh nahi, lekin tissue 'theek' karne ki ummeed na rakhein."

question.en: A patient says, "My physio told me I have poor posture so my back will wear out." What is the best response?
question.ur: Mareez kehta hai, "Mere physio ne kaha mere posture kharab hai isliye meri peeth ghis jayegi." Behtareen jawab kya hai?

text.en: Agree that the back will wear out and give a posture corrector
text.ur: Maan lein ke peeth ghis jayegi aur posture corrector dein

feedback.en: That reinforces fear and is not supported.
feedback.ur: Yeh khauf ko mazboot karta hai aur himayat shuda nahi.

text.en: Reassure that backs are strong and adaptable, that posture varies in healthy people, and that moving often and staying active are more helpful than holding a perfect posture
text.ur: Tasalli dein ke peeth mazboot aur dhalne wali hai, tandurust logon mein posture mukhtalif hoti hai, aur aksar hilna aur sargarm rehna perfect posture pakadne se zyada madadgar hai

feedback.en: Yes — it removes a scary belief without dismissing the person.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh insaan ko radd kiye baghair daraoni soch hatata hai.

text.en: Tell them posture is irrelevant and walk away
text.ur: Kahein posture ghair mutaliq hai aur chale jayein

feedback.ur: Position aaram ke liye ahem ho sakti hai.

question.en: Which claim about stretching is best supported?
question.ur: Stretching ke baare mein kaun sa daawa sab se behtar himayat shuda hai?

text.ur: Stretching sab ke liye nuqsan deh hai

feedback.ur: Yeh aam taur par mehfooz hai.

feedback.en: That claim goes beyond the evidence.
feedback.ur: Yeh daawa saboot se aage hai.

text.en: Stretching before or after exercise does not reliably prevent muscle soreness
text.ur: Exercise se pehle ya baad ki stretching dukhan ko pakke taur par nahi rokti

feedback.en: Yes — a Cochrane review found little or no effect on soreness.
feedback.ur: Haan — Cochrane review ne dukhan par kam ya koi asar nahi paya.

question.en: Why do myths like "poor posture causes damage" last for decades?
question.ur: "Kharab posture nuqsan paida karti hai" jaisi afwahein dehaiyon kyun tikti hain?

text.en: They contain a kernel of truth, sound sensible, are repeated by trusted people, and are rarely tested or corrected in everyday practice
text.ur: Un mein sachai ka daana hota hai, samajhdar lagti hain, bharosemand log dohrate hain, aur roz ki practice mein shayad hi aazmayi ya theek ki jati hain

feedback.ur: Haan — jaana pehchana hona sach jaisa lagta hai.

text.en: Because they have been proven many times
text.ur: Kyunke woh kai baar sabit ho chuki hain

feedback.en: The evidence is weak or mixed.

text.en: Because nobody is interested in them
text.ur: Kyunke koi in mein dilchaspi nahi rakhta

feedback.ur: Bohat si wasi taur par maani jati hain.

text.en: **Swapping one rigid rule for another.** Saying "posture does not matter at all" is as extreme as "posture matters above all". The honest message is "it matters a little, for some people, in some ways, and rarely in the way we feared". Another trap is mocking colleagues or patients for old beliefs: explain gently and keep the parts that help, such as moving more and building strength.
text.ur: **Ek sakht qaide ko doosre se badal dena.** "Posture bilkul ahem nahi" kehna utna hi intehai hai jitna "posture sab se ahem". Imaandar paigham hai "yeh thori ahem hai, kuch logon ke liye, kuch tareeqon se, aur shayad hi us tarah jis ka hum ne khauf kiya". Ek aur jaal purani soch par saathiyon ya mareezon ka mazaq udana hai: narmi se samjhayein aur woh hissay rakhein jo madad karte hain, jaise zyada harkat aur taqat banana.

text.en: **Replace fear with confidence.** Practise kind sentences such as "your back is strong", "pain does not always mean damage" and "movement is good for it". Avoid words like "wear and tear", "crooked", "out of place" or "unstable" without context, because they can make people anxious and cautious. Offer a plan: gradually more activity, strength work, regular changes of position and an agreed review.
text.ur: **Khauf ki jagah itminan dein.** "Aap ki peeth mazboot hai", "dard ka matlab hamesha nuqsan nahi" aur "harkat is ke liye achhi hai" jaise narm jumlon ki mashq karein. "Wear and tear", "tirchha", "jagah se hata hua" ya "ghair mustahkam" jaise alfaaz bina context ke na istemal karein, kyunke yeh logon ko pareshan aur mohtaat bana sakte hain. Plan dein: aahista zyada sargarmi, taqat ka kaam, position ka baqaida badalna aur tay shuda jaiza.

question.en: If posture matters so little, why do many people still feel better when they change it?
question.ur: Agar posture itni kam ahem hai to bohat se log phir bhi badalne par behtar kyun mehsoos karte hain?

answer.en: A change of position gives temporary relief, because any posture held too long becomes uncomfortable; the best posture is "the next one". Context matters too: attention, a calm explanation and the sense of doing something can reduce pain. So changing posture can help without proving that the old posture was damaging. Encourage variety rather than a "correct" posture.
answer.ur: Position badalne se waqti aaram milta hai, kyunke koi bhi posture jo bohat der pakri jaye takleef deh ho jati hai; behtareen posture "agla wala" hai. Context bhi ahem hai: tawajjo, pur-sukoon wazahat aur kuch karne ka ehsas dard kam kar sakte hain. Isliye posture badalna madad kar sakta hai bina yeh sabit kiye ke purani posture nuqsan deh thi. "Durust" posture ke bajaye harkat ki qismon ko farogh dein.

beats.patient: A 35-year-old accountant has had neck and upper back ache for three months. She was told by a previous therapist that her "rounded shoulders and forward head" are damaging her spine and she should wear a posture brace. She is anxious and avoids work.
beats.assessment: There is no evidence that her posture is causing damage, but her fear and inactivity are probably making things worse.
beats.treatment: The therapist explains that many pain-free people sit like her, suggests regular breaks and changes of position, a gradual strength programme and walking, and asks her to drop the brace.
beats.reassess: After six weeks her pain is lower, she works normally and her confidence has returned.

text.en: **Screen for red flags first.** Keep checking for serious causes, such as unexplained weight loss, night pain, fever, new neurological signs, a history of cancer or trauma. A myth-busting conversation never replaces assessment. And do not tell people that "nothing is wrong" when something may be: say "this pattern is common and usually settles, and here is what would make me worry".
text.ur: **Pehle red flags ki screening karein.** Seriyas wajuhaat ke liye jaanch jari rakhein, jaise be-wajah wazan kam hona, raat ka dard, bukhar, nayi neurological nishaniyan, cancer ya chot ki tareekh. Afwah todne wali baat cheet assessment ki jagah kabhi nahi leti. Aur logon se na kahein ke "kuch ghalat nahi" jab kuch ghalat ho sakta ho: kahein "yeh pattern aam hai aur aam taur par theek ho jata hai, aur yeh hai jo mujhe fikr mein daalega."

text.en: A commentary in the Journal of Orthopaedic and Sports Physical Therapy argued that the evidence for a link between sitting posture and back pain is weak, that a relatively wide range of postures is normal, and that advice to "sit up straight" can create fear and rigidity; it called for a shift towards variety of movement and reassurance. A Cochrane review of stretching to prevent or reduce muscle soreness after exercise found that stretching before or after exercise produced little or no clinically important reduction in soreness.
text.ur: Journal of Orthopaedic and Sports Physical Therapy ke ek tabsire ne daleel di ke baithne ki posture aur peeth dard ke beech talluq ka saboot kamzor hai, ke posture ki ek nisbatan wasi range normal hai, aur ke "seedha baithein" ka mashwara khauf aur sakhti paida kar sakta hai; is ne harkat ki qismon aur tasalli ki taraf tabdeeli ka mutalba kiya. Exercise ke baad muscle ki dukhan rokne ya kam karne ke liye stretching par ek Cochrane review ne paya ke exercise se pehle ya baad ki stretching ne dukhan mein kam ya koi clinical taur par ahem kami nahi di.

text.en: **Kernel, Overreach, Compare, Reassure.** Find the kernel of truth, spot the overreach, ask "compared with what?", and reassure.
text.ur: **Daana, Hadd se zyada, Muqabla, Tasalli.** Sachai ka daana dhoondhein, hadd se zyada pehchanein, "kis ke muqabale mein?" poochhein, aur tasalli dein.

summary.en: Posture, core stability, ergonomics, stretching and foam rolling are not useless, but they are less powerful and less specific than often claimed.
summary.ur: Posture, core stability, ergonomics, stretching aur foam rolling bekaar nahi, lekin aksar kiye jane wale daawon se kam taqatwar aur kam khaas hain.

summary.en: Variety of movement, strength and activity are safe, evidence-friendly messages; scary words can make pain worse.
summary.ur: Harkat ki qismein, taqat aur sargarmi mehfooz, saboot dost paighamat hain; daraone alfaaz dard barha sakte hain.

summary.en: Correct myths kindly, keep the helpful parts and always screen for red flags first.
summary.ur: Afwahein narmi se theek karein, mufeed hissay rakhein aur hamesha pehle red flags dekhein.

front.en: Is "poor posture" a strong cause of pain?
front.ur: Kya "kharab posture" dard ki mazboot wajah hai?

back.en: No; the link is weak and inconsistent.
back.ur: Nahi; talluq kamzor aur be-tarteeb hai.

front.en: Is core stability exercise better than other exercise for back pain?
front.ur: Kya core stability exercise peeth dard ke liye doosri exercise se behtar hai?

back.en: About the same; no single type is clearly best.
back.ur: Takreeban ek jaisi; koi ek qism saaf behtar nahi.

front.ur: Kya stretching dukhan ko pakke taur par rokti hai?

back.en: No; Cochrane found little or no effect.
back.ur: Nahi; Cochrane ne kam ya koi asar nahi paya.

front.en: What words can make people anxious about their backs?
front.ur: Kaun se alfaaz logon ko peeth ke baare mein pareshan kar sakte hain?

back.ur: "Wear and tear", "tirchha", "jagah se hata hua", "ghair mustahkam".

note.ur: Jaani pehchani nasihat sahi kyun lagti hai.
Mareezon ke liye narm, imaandar alfaaz.
